headline: Wednesday stays dry, then a fast-moving cold front brings bursts of heavy rain, gusty winds and possible thunderstorms late Wednesday night into Thursday, with about a quarter to half inch of rain in San Diego County and more to the north.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Wednesday stays dry after Monday night's widespread soaking west of the mountains, with temperatures near normal along the coast and below normal farther inland. A low cloud deck may form along the coast at times early Wednesday (20–30% chance, mainly about 2–7 AM), and high clouds spread in Wednesday morning, thickening again late Wednesday evening as the next storm approaches. Winds pick up over the mountains and deserts late Wednesday night, with a Wind Advisory starting at 11 PM for the San Bernardino Mountains and Apple and Lucerne Valleys; rain and possible isolated thunderstorms begin to arrive late Wednesday night.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: A storm diving down the West Coast pushes a cold front from northwest to southeast across the region starting Thursday morning; it is strongest in Orange and San Bernardino Counties and weakens as it reaches Riverside and San Diego Counties late Thursday morning or early afternoon, possibly with thunderstorms. Rain can fall at 0.25–0.50 inch per hour in San Diego County (heaviest in North County) and 0.50–0.65 inch per hour farther north and in the mountains, enough for street flooding and ponding on roads, along with 30–35 mph gusts at the coast and valleys, so secure outdoor items and watch for falling tree limbs; scattered showers linger through Thursday, and a weaker disturbance could bring more light rain to northern areas Friday (timing uncertain). Totals: 0.25–0.50 inch in San Diego County, 0.50–1 inch in Orange County and parts of the Inland Empire, 0.50–1.50 inches in the San Diego and Riverside mountains, 1–2 inches in the San Bernardino Mountains, 0.10–0.30 inch in the High Desert and 0.10 inch or less in the lower deserts. In the mountains and deserts, gusts of 50–60 mph hit the San Bernardino Mountains' ridges and desert slopes and 45–55 mph in the High Desert (Wind Advisory until 4 PM Thursday), and 40–55 mph in the Riverside and San Diego County mountains and passes, easing Thursday evening; snow levels stay above 7,000 feet during the heaviest rain, then drop to 6,000–6,500 feet Thursday afternoon and evening, with 3–5 inches above 7,500 feet and 1–2 inches below that.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Saturday looks dry, with temperatures staying near to below normal into early next week. Another round of unsettled weather is possible sometime Sunday or Monday, with most computer-model runs showing at least light rain west of the mountains. The timing and how far south that storm reaches are still uncertain, with more details expected in the coming days.

coast: A High Surf Advisory runs until 4 AM Wednesday for the Orange County and San Diego County coasts, and forecasters expect periods of high surf and coastal flooding with the unsettled weather this week. For boaters, a Small Craft Advisory runs until 4 AM Wednesday with 20–25 knot gusts and choppy 4–7 ft seas (steep 7–10 ft seas south of San Clemente Island through Wednesday morning), easing afterward. Conditions turn dangerous again Thursday into Friday morning, with steep 7–10 ft seas and 20–30 knot gusts, winds turning from south-southwest to west by late Thursday afternoon.
watch_for: Bursts of heavy rain and 30–35 mph gusts as the front passes Thursday morning and early afternoon, with street flooding possible.
Possible thunderstorms within the front on Thursday.
Timing of Friday's light showers and of the possible Sunday–Monday storm.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in a dry Wednesday and in Thursday's front, less sure about the timing of Friday's light showers, and uncertain about the timing and reach of the Sunday–Monday system.
